subject: Problem of RmaBackgroundCorrection in new aroma.affymetrix release

messages.author: c264a3d003b6a84f
messages.subject: Problem of RmaBackgroundCorrection in new aroma.affymetrix release
parts:
Hi,

I met a problem of using RmaBackgroundCorrection in the new release.
In the pase, I was using the following code to process the exon array
data, and it works well:
ds <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("GBM", chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2");
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HuEx-1_0-st-v2,full");
setCdf(ds, cdf);
dsBG <- bgAdjustRma(ds, name=getName(ds),
path=file.path("probeData",getName(ds), "RMABG"), addJitter=TRUE,
verbose=-2);
qn <- QuantileNormalization(dsBG, typesToUpdate="pm");

As the bgAdjustRma() was deprecated is the new version, I used the
follow function instead:
dsBG <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(ds, addJitter=TRUE, jitterSd=0.2);
qn <- QuantileNormalization(dsBG, typesToUpdate="pm");

This function seems failed, and cannot be pass to the next step of
normalization:
> qn <- QuantileNormalization(dsBG, typesToUpdate="pm");
Error in list("QuantileNormalization(dsBG, typesToUpdate = "pm")" =
<environment>, :
[2007-07-17 08:16:17] Exception: Argument 'dataSet' is not an
AffymetrixCelSet object: RmaBackgroundCorrection
at throw(Exception(...))
at throw.default("Argument 'dataSet' is not an AffymetrixCelSet
object: ", cla
at throw("Argument 'dataSet' is not an AffymetrixCelSet object: ",
class(dataS
at Transform(...)
at extend(Transform(...), "ProbeLevelTransform")
at ProbeLevelTransform(...)
at extend(ProbeLevelTransform(...),
"QuantileNormalization", .subsetToUpdate =
at QuantileNormalization(dsBG, typesToUpdate = "pm")
> dsBG
RmaBackgroundCorrection:
Data set: GBM
Input tags:
Output tags: RBC
Number of arrays: 51 (3215.19MB)
Chip type: HuEx-1_0-st-v2
Algorithm parameters: (subsetToUpdate: NULL, typesToUpdate: chr "pm",
addJitter: logi FALSE, jitterSd: num 0.2, pmonly: logi TRUE)
Output path: probeData/GBM,RBC/HuEx-1_0-st-v2
Is done: FALSE
RAM: 0.00MB

I have tried different usages of RmaBackgroundCorrection. However,
even the base useage like
dsBG <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(ds);
failed. Is there anything wrong of my using RmaBackgroundCorrection?

Your help is greatly appreciated.

Ju

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Problem of RmaBackgroundCorrection in new aroma.affymetrix release
parts:
Hi,

Both RmaBackgroundCorrection and QuantileNormalization are so called
Transform classes (inheriting from this superclass). When you define
objects of these, e.g. via constructor RmaBackgroundCorrection(), you
will only setup a Transform object, but you will not perform any
preprocessing. In order to do this, you have to call the process()
method which returns a transformed AffymetrixCelSet, which is what you
want.

Please see subsection "Calibration and normalization of probe-level
data" under "Pages" on the aroma.affymetrix group site. See also the
examples.

Cheers

Henrik
